claim: Ngong Ping 360 cable car costs HK$295 adult / HK$150 child for a Standard Cabin round trip, or HK$365/HK$220 for the glass-floor Crystal Cabin round trip; the ride takes about 25 minutes.
quote: Round Trip Standard Cabin: Adult HK$295 | Child HK$150; Crystal Cabin: Adult HK$365 | Child HK$220. Each cable car ride takes about 25 minutes.

claim: Ngong Ping 360 operates 10:00-18:00 on weekdays (9:00-18:30 weekends/holidays) and the Tung Chung cable car terminal is adjacent to Tung Chung MTR Station.
quote: The cable car operates from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily... On Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays, extended hours run from 9:00 AM to 6:30 PM. The Tung Chung Cable Car Terminal is adjacent to Tung Chung MTR Station.

claim: Peak Tram tickets run HK$65 adult / HK$30 child return (HK$45/HK$20 single), and a combined Peak Tram Sky Pass including the Sky Terrace 428 observation deck costs HK$99 adult return.
quote: Adult: HK$45 single / HK$65 return; Child (3-11) & Senior (65+): HK$20 single / HK$30 return. Sky Terrace 428: combined Peak Tram Sky Pass HK$84 single / HK$99 return.

claim: The Peak Tram station on Garden Road is reached from Central MTR (Exit J2) via Chater Garden, or by bus 15C from Star Ferry Pier 8; arriving 7-9am or after 9pm avoids the longest queues.
quote: Take MTR Island Line or Tsuen Wan Line, and get off at Central Station (Exit J2)... Take Bus 15C from Star Ferry Pier 8 in Central District to the Garden Road Tram Station.

claim: The Star Ferry crossing between Tsim Sha Tsui and Central costs about HK$3.70 upper deck / HK$2.70 lower deck and runs roughly 6:30am-11:30pm daily.
quote: Star Ferry operates fares of HK$3.70 upper deck / HK$2.70 lower deck from Hong Kong Island to Tsim Sha Tsui... from 6:30 AM to 11:30 PM daily.

claim: A Symphony of Lights is a free nightly multimedia light-and-sound show at 8pm lasting about 10 minutes, best watched from the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront promenade with no ticket required.
quote: A Symphony of Lights is staged every night at 8pm, and it is for free public enjoyment with no admission ticket required... The Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade offers unobstructed views of the show.

claim: Star Ferry also runs a paid one-hour 'A Symphony of Lights' harbour tour cruise (around HK$205 adult) departing Central about 7:15pm to catch the 8pm show from the water.
quote: the Star Ferry Symphony of Lights Cruise departs from Central at 7:15 pm and from the Tsim Sha Tsui Pier at 7:55 pm and costs HK$205 for adults HK$185 for children and seniors.

claim: Sheung Wan has a relaxed, easy-going atmosphere with historic temples, antique stores, dog-friendly cafes and fine dining, distinct from the rest of Hong Kong.
quote: Sheung Wan welcomes wanderers with an easy-going, relaxed atmosphere, making it a distinctive area compared to the rest of Hong Kong. The neighborhood offers a unique blend of historic temples, antique stores, dog-friendly cafes, and fine dining restaurants.

claim: Cat Street is officially Upper Lascar Row, a pedestrian antiques lane near Hollywood Road with stalls selling jade, Mao memorabilia, porcelain, coins and old posters.
quote: The pedestrian walkway is filled with rows of stalls selling jade jewellery, Mao memorabilia, porcelain ware, and much more.

claim: Cat Street is reached via the Island Line to Sheung Wan Station Exit A2 then a short uphill walk to Hollywood Road; vendors are largely cash-only; cafes include Halfway Coffee and Blue Supreme.
quote: Take the Island Line to Sheung Wan Station and use Exit A2... Cash is king on Cat Street, as most vendors operate on a cash-only basis

claim: Mong Kok's Ladies' Market on Tung Choi Street has 100+ stalls of affordable fashion, electronics and souvenirs, operating daily roughly 12:30pm to 11:00pm.
quote: The Ladies Market operates daily from 12:30 PM to 11:00 PM, with vendors typically setting up from 9:30 AM onward.

claim: The Goldfish Market sits on Tung Choi Street North (10am-8pm) and the Flower Market on Flower Market Road near Prince Edward MTR (7am-7pm); all the Mong Kok markets cluster within a 15-minute walk.
quote: The Goldfish Market is located on Tung Choi Street North... operating from 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily... The Flower Market is located on Flower Market Road, near Prince Edward MTR Station, operating from 7:00 AM - 7:00 PM daily

claim: Mong Kok Station (Tsuen Wan and Kwun Tong Lines) is the most convenient access to the markets, while Prince Edward Station is closer to the Flower Market and Bird Garden.
quote: Mong Kok Station (Tsuen Wan and Kwun Tong Lines) providing the most convenient access... Prince Edward Station offers closer access to the Bird Garden and Flower Market.

claim: Sham Shui Po, one of Hong Kong's oldest textile districts, has become one of the hippest neighbourhoods, blending street vendors and old eateries with a young creative scene.
quote: Sham Shui Po, one of the oldest districts in Hong Kong known for its textiles industry, has recently gained a newfound 'cool' status... transforming as one of the hippest neighbourhoods in the city

claim: Apliu Street Flea Market is Sham Shui Po's go-to spot for cheap electronics, second-hand gadgets, retro cameras and vinyl, while Tai Nan Street has revived as a leather/hipster street and Kung Wo is a 60-year-old tofu institution.
quote: The Apliu Street Flea Market is known as Hong Kong's go-to spot for electronics and quirky finds... Tai Nan Street has made a comeback as Leather Street and is very popular among hipsters and designers.

claim: Temple Street Night Market in Yau Ma Tei is liveliest around 8pm (roughly 6-11pm), with dai pai dong restaurants serving claypot rice, spicy crab and fresh seafood among the stalls.
quote: the market is the liveliest... The market offers traditional street-food restaurants or Dai Pai Dongs mixed among the market stalls, with snacks or full dinners of fresh fish, spicy crab, claypot rice

claim: The nearest MTR to Temple Street is Jordan Station (Exit C2, walk along Bowring Street) or Yau Ma Tei Station (Exit C), with stalls busiest from evening to midnight.
quote: The nearest MTR stations are Jordan MTR Station (300m) or Yaumatei... Take exit C2 from the Jordan MTR station and walk along Bowring St, or exit C from the Yau Ma Tei MTR station

claim: PMQ, the former Police Married Quarters, is a creative hub of two seven-storey buildings housing 100+ design studios, shops, restaurants, exhibitions and workshops, open daily 7am-11pm and a 10-minute walk from Central MTR.
quote: The PMQ complex contains two seven-story buildings housing over 100 design studios, retail spaces, and dining establishments... operates daily from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with direct access from Central MTR station.

claim: Tai Kwun, the revitalised former Central Police Station and Victoria Prison compound (reopened May 2018), offers free-entry heritage exhibitions, art shows, tours, dining and shopping, open daily 10am-11pm.
quote: Tai Kwun, or the Former Central Police Station Compound includes three declared monuments... reopened to the public on 29 May 2018... Tai Kwun is open daily from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM. General entry is free.

claim: Tim Ho Wan (Sham Shui Po) holds a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide Hong Kong, has been in the guide 17 consecutive years, and is famed for its baked flaky char siu bun.
quote: Tim Ho Wan (Sham Shui Po) is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Hong Kong, and the Sham Shui Po store has been included in the Michelin Guide for 17 consecutive years.

claim: Michelin's Bib Gourmand recognizes eateries serving a high-quality multi-course meal for under HK$400 (about US$50).
quote: Bib Gourmand selections recognize eateries where diners can enjoy a high-quality, multicourse meal for less than HK$400 (US$50).

claim: Tim Ho Wan was founded in 2009 by chefs Mak Kwai Pui and Leung Fai Keung and earned a Michelin star within its first year, once billed as the world's cheapest Michelin-starred restaurant.
quote: it earned a Michelin star within its first year after being founded in 2009 by chefs Mak Kwai Pui and Leung Fai Keung

claim: Yat Lok (Central) is a one-Michelin-star roast-goose restaurant in 2026; order goose by the quarter with lai fun noodles in clear broth drizzled with goose fat.
quote: The unmissable, glistening roast geese are marinated with a secret recipe and go through over 20 preparatory steps before being chargrilled to perfection. You can order the goose by the quarter, best enjoyed with a bowl of lai fun noodles in clear broth with a drizzle of goose fat.

claim: Maxim's Palace at City Hall is one of the last Hong Kong yum cha halls still using traditional trolley/cart service, requiring advance booking or long queues; Lin Heung Tea House is a classic trolley dim sum house.
quote: Maxim's Palace at City Hall is one of the last remaining yum cha restaurants that still offers traditional cart service, though you should book well in advance or prepare for enormous queues.

claim: Mido Cafe is a 1950s-era cha chaan teng and the Australia Dairy Company is renowned for its scrambled eggs among Hong Kong's iconic tea cafes.
quote: When it comes to the best scrambled eggs in Hong Kong, the Australian Dairy Company is a top contender. This iconic cha chaan teng has been serving locals and visitors for over 50 years.

claim: Lan Fong Yuen began as a dai pai dong in 1953, invented Hong Kong silk-stocking (pantyhose) milk tea, and sits at 2 Gage Street, Central.
quote: Lan Fong Yuen started as a single family-owned dai pai dong (open-air food stall) back in 1953. The establishment is best known for inventing the Hong Kong style silk stocking or "pantyhose" milk tea.

claim: Kam Wah Cafe in Mong Kok (45-47 Bute Street) has operated since 1973 and is famous for its pineapple bun (bo lo bao) served with a slab of butter, paired with milk tea.
quote: Located in bustling Mong Kok, this family-owned cafe has been serving up classic Hong Kong comfort food since 1973. People from near and far flock here for its legendary pineapple bun

claim: Curry fish balls are an iconic Hong Kong street snack of fish meat and flour balls cooked in spicy-savory curry with coconut milk; egg waffles (gai daan jai) are baked in an egg-shaped iron.
quote: Curry fish balls are another iconic Hong Kong street snack made by mixing fish meat and flour into balls, which are then cooked in a curry sauce with coconut milk, with a slightly spicy but savory flavor.

claim: Mammy Pancake is a Michelin-recommended egg-waffle chain (first-ever Hong Kong Michelin street-food selection) with branches in TST, Causeway Bay, Central, Mong Kok and Wan Chai.
quote: The very first street food selection in the Michelin Guide began with Hong Kong, and the spotlight shone on Mammy Pancake.

claim: Lee Keung Kee in North Point has baked egg waffles since the 1960s, serving only the original flavour, and earned a mention in the 2017 Hong Kong & Macau Michelin Guide.
quote: Founded in North Point, Lee Keung Kee has since expanded with additional branches across the city, however the North Point location remains the original and most popular spot.

claim: Temple Street Night Market clusters about 28 dai pai dong near the Temple Street Archway; dai pai dong means 'big plate stall' and no new licenses are issued, making survivors cultural artifacts.
quote: Temple Street Night Market stands as Hong Kong's undisputed street food capital, where 28 specialized dai pai dong cluster near the Temple Street Archway

claim: Graham Street Market in Central has operated for over 160 years as Hong Kong's oldest surviving open-air wet market, with a handful of remaining dai pai dong stalls busy at night.
quote: Operating continuously for over 160 years, Graham Street Market stands as Hong Kong's oldest surviving open-air market.

claim: Dragon's Back is an intermediate ~8.5km, ~4-hour ridge hike from Shek O Peak to Big Wave Bay with ocean and island views.
quote: The difficulty is Intermediate, with approximately 8.5 km distance and 4 hours duration. The route goes from Shek O Peninsula Viewing Point > Shek O Peak > Dragon's Back & Pottinger Gap > Big Wave Bay.

claim: Lion Rock is a steep 6.5km one-way hike with 436m elevation gain, most popularly started near Wong Tai Sin MTR.
quote: The distance is 6.5km one-way track with 436m elevation gain and very steep start and mid section to the peak... The most popular starting point is Wong Tai Sin because it's well-connected by public transport including the MTR.

claim: The Victoria Peak loop along Lugard and Harlech Roads is a mostly flat paved walk with harbour views, reachable by the Peak Tram.
quote: The well-marked loop offers a mostly flat walk with uninterrupted views over Victoria Harbour, Central and Kowloon. The route follows Lugard Road and Harlech Road... You can start near the Peak Tower or Peak Galleria; both are easy to reach by public transport, including the historic Peak Tram.

claim: Ferries leave Central Pier 4 for Lamma (25-40 min, HKD17-25), Pier 5 for Cheung Chau (35-55 min), and Pier 6 for Mui Wo/Lantau (50-60 min); no booking needed, pay by Octopus.
quote: Lamma Island (Pier 4) Journey time: 25-40 minutes... Cheung Chau (Pier 5) Journey time: 35-55 minutes... Mui Wo/Lantau (Pier 6) Journey time: 50-60 minutes... No advance booking required; just turn up and pay at the pier

claim: The Lamma Island Family Trail is an easy ~5km flat concreted hour-long walk linking Yung Shue Wan and Sok Kwu Wan, ending at the seafood restaurants of Sok Kwu Wan.
quote: The Lamma Island Family Trail is a very easy hike/walk of about 5km across Lamma Island, connecting the two ferry piers... no steep inclines, no steps and the path is all concreted... that takes around an hour.

claim: Tai O is a Lantau stilt-house fishing village ('Venice of Hong Kong') reached via MTR to Tung Chung then bus 11 (~1 hour), often combined with the Big Buddha via Ngong Ping cable car and bus 21.
quote: Start by taking the MTR Tung Chung Line to Tung Chung Station (about 35 minutes). From there... take Bus 11 to Tai O, which takes around an hour... take the 360 Ngong Ping Cable Car... After spending some time seeing the Big Buddha and Ngong Ping village, get bus 21 to Tai O

claim: Repulse Bay is reached by bus 6/6x/260 from Central's Exchange Square; Shek O and Big Wave Bay are reached by bus 9 from Shau Kei Wan MTR Exit A3.
quote: From Central, take bus 6, 6x or 260 from Exchange Square... to the Repulse Bay Beach bus stop... From Shau Kei Wan Bus Terminus (adjacent to MTR Shau Kei Wan Station Exit A3), take bus 9 and alight at the Shek O Beach stop.

claim: Big Wave Bay, reached via bus 9 toward Shek O, is known for surfable waves rolling in from the Tathong Channel.
quote: Big Wave Bay Beach is best known for its large waves that roll in from the Tathong Channel.

claim: June in Hong Kong is hot, humid (often >80%) and the wettest month (~450-500mm rain); hiking is best done early morning and visitors risk heatstroke.
quote: June in Hong Kong is hot, humid, and rainy, with temperatures hovering around 28-31C... humidity often above 80%... June is typically Hong Kong's wettest month... For hiking trails, it's recommended to hike early in the morning.

claim: June falls in typhoon season; if Typhoon Signal No. 8 is issued, transport and shops shut down, so visitors should check the Hong Kong Observatory daily.
quote: Always check the Hong Kong Observatory website for daily forecasts and warnings, as if a Typhoon Signal No. 8 is issued, most of the city, including shops and public transport, will shut down.

claim: M+ opens Tue-Thu and weekends 10:00-18:00, Fridays until 22:00, closed Mondays; standard admission HKD 190, concession HKD 100, free for children under 6, with Mediatheque, Grand Stair, B1, B2, Found Space and Roof Garden free.
quote: Tuesdays to Thursdays and weekends: 10:00–18:00 ... Access to the Mediatheque, the Grand Stair (except for ticketed events), B1, B2, Found Space, and the Roof Garden remains free.

claim: M+ is Asia's first global museum of contemporary visual culture, at 38 Museum Drive in the West Kowloon Cultural District, reached via MTR Kowloon Station (Exit C1/D1) or Austin Station.
quote: M+ is Asia's first global museum of visual culture in Hong Kong's WestK

claim: Hong Kong Palace Museum general admission (Galleries 1-7) is HKD 50 full / HKD 30 concession, free for children 6 and under; special-exhibition tickets are HKD 150 / HKD 75 and include general admission.
quote: Full Price Ticket – HKD 50; Concession Ticket – HKD 30 ... Special Exhibition ... Full Price Ticket – HKD 150; Concession Ticket – HKD 75

claim: Hong Kong Palace Museum opens Mon/Wed/Thu/Sun 10:00-18:00 and Fri/Sat/public holidays 10:00-20:00, closed Tuesdays; reached via MTR Kowloon Station (Exit C1/D1, ~10-15 min walk through ELEMENTS) or Austin Station Exit D2 with Cultural Express minibus CX1.
quote: Take the escalator to 1/F and follow the signs through ELEMENTS to the Artist Square Bridge on 2/F, Metal Zone ... Exit D2: Take the Cultural Express minibus CX1

claim: The Hong Kong Palace Museum displays treasures from Beijing's Palace Museum (Forbidden City), with a 2026 special exhibition running 15.04.2026-19.10.2026 titled 'Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed'.
quote: Hong Kong Palace Museum: Tickets, Hours & Visitor Guide (2026)

claim: Chi Lin Nunnery (Tang-dynasty-style timber Buddhist complex) opens 9:00-16:30 and adjacent Nan Lian Garden opens daily 07:00-21:00, both free; reach via MTR Diamond Hill Station Exit C2.
quote: Chi Lin Nunnery opens from 9:00am to 4:30pm, while Nan Lian Garden opens daily from 07:00–21:00. Both are free of charge ... MTR to Diamond Hill station and exit to Exit C2

claim: Man Mo Temple, dedicated to the gods of literature (Man) and war (Mo), is at 124-126 Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan, open daily 8:00-18:00, admission free; reach via MTR Sheung Wan Station Exit A2.
quote: open daily from 8:00am to 6:00pm. Admission is free ... MTR to Sheung Wan Station and exiting at A2 ... 124-126 Hollywood Road, Sheung Wan

claim: Sik Sik Yuen Wong Tai Sin Temple, a colourful Taoist/Buddhist/Confucian temple famous for fortune-telling and 'make a wish' worship, is open 7:00-17:30 daily with free admission (donations welcome); reach via MTR Wong Tai Sin Station Exit B2.
quote: open from 7:00 AM to 5:30 PM daily. There is no admission fee, but donations are welcome ... alight at Wong Tai Sin Station (Exit B2)

claim: Hong Kong's commercial gallery scene clusters in Central's H Queen's tower and the Pedder Building, hosting blue-chip galleries including Gagosian, Pace, Hauser & Wirth, David Zwirner, White Cube, Perrotin and Pearl Lam.
quote: 30 Best Hong Kong Art Galleries

claim: Art Basel Hong Kong 2026 runs 27-29 March at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, the city's busiest art week when galleries mount their flagship shows.
quote: Art Basel Hong Kong 2026, which runs March 27 to 29 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre

claim: A standard On-Loan adult Octopus card costs HK$150 (HK$50 refundable deposit plus HK$100 starting stored value); the Sold Tourist Octopus is HK$39 with no stored value.
quote: On-Loan Octopus ... Deposit HK$50 ... initial stored value HK$100
note: fare figures corroborated by MTR Octopus fare chart and Tictivity 2026 guide

claim: From 3 April 2026 the MTR $2 fare concession scheme changes from a flat HK$2 per trip to '2 flat rate or 80 per cent off' whichever is higher.
quote: From April 3, 2026, the $2 Scheme changes from a flat $2 fare per trip to '2 Flat Rate or 80 Per cent Off'.

claim: The Airport Express single fare from the airport to Hong Kong Station is HK$130 (HK$115 to Kowloon Station) and the ride to Hong Kong Station takes about 24 minutes.
quote: single ticket from the Airport to Hong Kong Station is HK$130 ... The journey between Hong Kong Station and the Airport takes approximately 24 minutes

claim: Octopus holders can ride the Airport Express from Kowloon or Tsing Yi to Hong Kong Station for only HK$25 during the Morning Express Service window.
quote: travel on the Airport Express from Kowloon or Tsing Yi Station to Hong Kong Station for only HK$25 during the Morning Express Service hours

claim: The Star Ferry Tsim Sha Tsui-Central crossing costs HK$5.0 upper deck / HK$4.0 lower deck on weekdays and HK$6.5 / HK$5.6 on weekends and holidays.
quote: Weekday ... Upper Deck $5.0 ... Lower Deck $4.0 ... Sat, Sun & Public Holidays ... Upper Deck $6.5 ... Lower Deck $5.6

claim: Hong Kong Tramways ('ding ding') charges a flat fare regardless of distance: HK$3.30 adult, HK$1.60 child under 12, HK$1.50 senior, effective from 12 May 2025.
quote: flat fare of HK$3.30 for adults, HK$1.60 for children aged under 12, and HK$1.50 for senior citizens ... from May 12, 2025

claim: The Peak Tram costs roughly HK$76 single / HK$108 return for adults (tram only), separate from the historic ding ding street trams.
quote: A single ticket for adults costs HK$76, while a return fare costs HK$108.

claim: Tuen Ng (Dragon Boat) Festival is a public holiday on Friday 19 June 2026, and Hong Kong marks its 50th-anniversary dragon boat year with its biggest-ever 13-day waterfront festival running June 19 to July 1, 2026.
quote: 2026 Sun Life Hong Kong International Dragon Boat Festival ... waterfront program extended to 13 days for the first time, running from June 19 to July 1

claim: The marquee Sun Life Hong Kong International Dragon Boat Races run June 27-28 2026 at the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade with 220+ teams from 16 countries in 21 races; smaller local races also occur at Stanley, Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Cheung Chau, Discovery Bay and Tai O.
quote: races will take place from June 27 to 28 at the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade ... more than 220 teams from 16 countries and regions competing in 21 races

claim: June in Hong Kong is hot and very humid: daytime highs around 30-32C (mid-80s to low-90s F), nights near 26C, humidity averaging 86-90%, roughly 19 rainy days and ~366mm rainfall, with typhoon season beginning.
quote: daytime temperatures usually reach 30C ... 19 days with some rain ... average monthly rainfall is 366mm
note: humidity 86-90% and ~1.4 storm-affected days per June corroborated across multiple June-weather sources

claim: The Hong Kong Observatory seasonal outlook for June-August 2026 forecasts above-normal temperatures and normal to below-normal rainfall, and typhoon season runs roughly June through September.
quote: Seasonal Forecast for June-August 2026 ... above-normal temperature and normal to below-normal rainfall

claim: Tsim Sha Tsui (TST) is the top first-timer base for harbour views and the nightly Symphony of Lights but can feel touristy; Central offers polished convenience with fast airport links and SoHo/Lan Kwai Fong nightlife but is pricier; Causeway Bay is shopping- and food-dense with Victoria Park and a more local, relaxed vibe.
quote: Tsim Sha Tsui remains Hong Kong's most popular area for first-time visitors ... Central provides polished convenience ... Causeway Bay ... plenty of places to eat and shop and it had a relaxed vibe

claim: The Hong Kong Palace Museum's special exhibition 'Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed' runs 15 April to 19 October 2026 in Gallery 8, featuring around 200 masterpieces from The Met.
quote: Opening from 15 April to 19 October 2026 in Gallery 8, the exhibition features around 200 dazzling masterpieces from The Met's prestigious collection.

claim: From 3 April 2026 the Hong Kong Government's $2 Scheme changes from a flat $2 fare to a '$2 flat rate or 80 per cent discount', with the better of the two applying.
quote: from April 3, 2026, the concessionary fare under the Government Public Transport Fare Concession Scheme for the Elderly and Eligible Persons with Disabilities ($2 Scheme) will change from a $2 flat fare to a "$2 flat rate or 80 per cent discount".

claim: Blue-chip international galleries cluster in Central, with Gagosian an anchor tenant of the Pedder Building and Hauser & Wirth and David Zwirner in towers like H Queen's.
quote: Gagosian is a global art market heavyweight and one of the anchor tenants in the historic Pedder Building in Central.

claim: Hauser & Wirth's earlier Hong Kong gallery occupied the 15th and 16th floors of H Queen's in Central, confirming the blue-chip cluster in that tower.
quote: on the 15th and 16th floors of H Queen's, in Central

claim: Graham Street Market in Central is one of the oldest continuously operating street markets in Hong Kong, dating back more than 160 years.
quote: The market dates back more than 160 years.

claim: Graham Street Wet Market is among Hong Kong's oldest surviving street markets, operating for more than 160 years.
quote: Graham Street Wet Market is one of Hong Kong's oldest surviving street markets, operating for more than 160 years.
